Based on the evidence collected, I can now provide the enriched candidate analysis. The key finding is that the `_fork` function executes browser commands through a shell with URL substitution, creating a command injection vulnerability.

{
  "candidate_id": "candidate-4",
  "filepath": "canto_curses/guibase.py",
  "changed_line": 273,
  "statement": "pid = self._fork(browser[\"path\"], url, browser[\"text\"], fetch)",
  "function_name": "_goto",
  "operation_type": "function_call",
  "source_summary": "URLs come from user navigation commands; browser path comes from configuration (CantoCurses.browser.path via remote one-config)",
  "sink_summary": "os.execv(\"/bin/sh\", [\"/bin/sh\", \"-c\", path]) where path contains browser command with URL substitution",
  "guard_summary": "No input validation or sanitization on URL before substitution into shell command; browser configuration is trusted without validation",
  "risk_pattern": "User-controlled URL directly substituted into browser command template and executed via shell without proper escaping or validation",
  "used_variable_sources": ["browser[\"path\"] from configuration", "url from user input", "browser[\"text\"] from configuration"],
  "called_function_context": ["_fork(path, href, text, fetch) executes: path.replace(\"%u\", href) -> encoder(path) -> os.execv(\"/bin/sh\", [\"/bin/sh\", \"-c\", path])"],
  "enclosing_conditions": ["if browser[\"path\"]: (line 265)", "for url in urls: (line 272)", "if fetch: (line 88 for file download)"],
  "context_summary": "The _goto function takes user-provided URLs and passes them to _fork, which substitutes URLs into browser command templates and executes them via shell",
  "unresolved_facts": ["Exact default browser command configuration", "Whether browser path configuration is user-configurable", "Specific validation in configuration loading process"]
}
